sentences.text: Naashoibitosaurus is classified as a saurolophine hadrosaurid, a type of flat-headed or solid-crested duckbill dinosaur. It belongs to the subfamily Saurolophinae and is most closely related to solid-crested hadrosaurids like Saurolophus.
This large herbivore was capable of moving on two or four legs.
Its mouth contained continuously replacing teeth packed into dental batteries holding hundreds of teeth, with only a few in use at any given time.
The dinosaur used a broad beak to crop plants and cheek-like organs to hold food, allowing it to feed on vegetation ranging from the ground up to approximately 4 meters (13 feet) high.
Naashoibitosaurus lived approximately 73 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous, and its fossils were found in the Kirtland Formation of the San Juan Basin in New Mexico, United States.

To date, only a partial skeleton has been discovered. David Gillette and David Thomas collected the type specimen, believing it came from the Naashoibito Member of the Kirtland Formation, but it was actually collected from the older, late Campanian-age De-na-zin Member.
Jack Horner first described the type specimen as belonging to the genus Kritosaurus. In 1992, he described the skull specifically as belonging to an immature Kritosaurus.

Later, Hunt and Lucas initially described the postcranial bones as belonging to Edmontosaurus saskatchewanensis. They assigned the specimen its own generic name, Naashoibitosaurus, after realizing the skull did not match Edmontosaurus and Kritosaurus was indeterminate.
Thomas Williamson challenged the separation of Naashoibitosaurus and Kritosaurus in 2000. He supported Horner's argument that nasal crests in hadrosaurines move backward on the skull during growth.

Naashoibitosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Campanian stage, approximately 73 million years ago. The time range for the taxon is estimated from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
A 2014 study concluded that while Naashoibitosaurus is similar to Kritosaurus, it represents a distinct species.
